fest.name: TechNation
fest.venue: Shree Damodar Educational Campus, G R Kare Road, Tansor, Comba, Margao, Salcete, Goa 403601

general: Participation Eligibility
- Participation in TechNation 2027 is by invitation to recognised colleges and institutions across India.
- The event is open to undergraduate students pursuing BCA, B.Sc. (Computer Science/IT), B.Voc. (Software Technologies/Software Development), or other equivalent IT-related undergraduate programmes.
- Participating institutions must be recognised by UGC / AICTE / State or Central Universities or other competent statutory authorities.
- Participants must be bona fide students of their respective college/institution.
Outstation Team Accommodation
- Outstation teams are requested to confirm participation well in advance (by 15th December 2026) to facilitate logistical arrangements.
- Accommodation arrangements shall be dependent on the type of registration chosen by the participating teams.

- Type I Registration: Without Stay/Accommodation (Registration Fee ₹3,000/-). Accommodation arrangements shall be the responsibility of the participating teams; however, the organising committee may provide limited assistance and guidance upon prior request by 17th December 2026.

- Type II Registration: With Stay/Accommodation (Registration Fee ₹6,000/-). The host institution shall arrange accommodation for 2 nights, subject to registration confirmation by 15th December 2026. Check-in: 07th January 2027 (after 2.00 pm); check-out: 09th January 2027 (by 11.00 am).
- Local transportation between the designated hotel (place of stay) and the event venue, and vice versa, will be arranged by the host institution.
- Any other travel and stay expenses for outstation participants, beyond what is described above, shall be borne by the participating institution/team.
- Working breakfast and working lunch on 08th and 09th January 2027 will be provided by the host institution at the venue.
- For accommodation assistance/information, please contact:
- Dr. Sameer Patil – Assistant Professor (09.00 am to 5.00 pm)
- Mobile/WhatsApp: 75077 20245
- Email: samir.patil@vvm.edu.in
Registration, Participation and Team Composition
- The team registration fee is as follows:
- Teams within Goa: ₹3,000 (Rupees Three Thousand Only)
- Out-of-state teams without stay/accommodation: ₹3,000 (Rupees Three Thousand Only)
- Out-of-state teams with 2-day stay/accommodation: ₹6,000 (Rupees Six Thousand Only)
- The last date to register (only in online mode) is Tuesday, 15th December 2026, by 3.00 pm.
- The event will be conducted offline at the host college campus on 08th and 09th January 2027, as mentioned in the information brochure.
- Participation is limited to one team per college/institution.
- Each team must comprise 10 students, all from the same institution.
- Teams may assign different participants for different events to avoid schedule conflicts.
Registration Formalities

- Each team must have a Student Team Leader and be accompanied by a Faculty Coordinator. The Faculty Coordinator's physical presence is optional for teams within Goa but compulsory for outstation teams.
- A deputation letter issued by the participating institution, along with valid college ID cards of all participants, must be produced at the registration desk on 08th January 2027.
- Teams must confirm their participation at least 15 to 20 days before the event dates.
Team Identity & Anonymity Rules
- Each team will be assigned a unique Team Name by the host institution at the venue on 08th January (or earlier, during online registration), which must be used for participation in all events.
- To ensure fair and unbiased evaluation, institution identity must not be disclosed by the participants during the event.

- Wearing, displaying, or carrying any college/institution-identifying name, logo, insignia, or branded material in any form is strictly prohibited. This anonymity rule is enforced from desk registration on 08th January until the announcement of results at the valedictory function on 09th January 2027.
- Any violation of the non-disclosure policy may lead to penalties, disqualification from specific events, or overall disqualification, as decided by the organising committee.
Communication
- All official communication, including event schedules, rules, updates, and announcements, will be shared via the registered email ID of the Team Leader or Faculty Coordinator.
- Any additional event-specific instructions will be communicated prior to the start of the event.
Code of Conduct
- All participants must strictly adhere to the Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and campus regulations during the event.
- Offensive language, misconduct, or vulgar behaviour in any form will result in immediate disqualification of the team.
- Participants should maintain professionalism, discipline, and ethical conduct throughout the event.
Event Rules & Judgement
- Each event will have specific rules, which must be followed strictly.
- The decisions of the judges and organising committee shall be final and binding in all matters.
- No appeals or disputes will be entertained.
Evaluation & Scoring
- Points will be awarded based on participation and positions secured in individual events.
- First and Second Prize winners of each event will receive trophies and e-certificates (or printed certificates).
- The results of all the individual events shall be declared during the valedictory ceremony.
- Based on cumulative points, Overall Winner and Overall Runner-Up trophies and certificates will be awarded at the valedictory ceremony.
General Provisions
- Any clarification regarding specific events may be obtained from the respective Student Event Heads in advance.
- The organising committee reserves the right to make modifications to the schedule or rules, if necessary, in the interest of smooth conduct of the event.
dayOf: Produce the deputation letter from your institution and valid college ID cards of all participants at the registration desk on 8 January 2027.
Every team is assigned a unique Team Name at the venue; use it in all events. Institution identity must not be disclosed.
No college name, logo, insignia or branded material may be worn, displayed or carried, from desk registration until the results are announced at the valedictory on 9 January 2027.
Breakfast and lunch on both days are provided by the host institution at the venue.
Follow the SOPs and campus regulations. Offensive language, misconduct or vulgar behaviour means immediate disqualification of the team.
Judges' and organising committee decisions are final. Results are declared at the valedictory ceremony, where the Overall Winner and Overall Runner-Up trophies are awarded on cumulative points.

competitions.name: Reel-O-Tech
competitions.subtitle: Reel Making Competition
competitions.rounds: Shoot on Day 1 · Submit on Day 2
competitions.tagline: Capture Day 1 on campus and turn it into a reel the whole fest will watch.
competitions.overview: Participants must create an engaging reel video based on the glimpses of Day 1. The reel must be posted on your personal Instagram account, tagging the college's official account (@damodar_college), and must contain all the moments of Day 1 within the campus.
competitions.statement: Shoot within the campus on 8 January and submit the finished reel on Day 2 (9 January) at 10 AM sharp.
rules: The reel must exclusively feature moments captured on Day 1 of TechNation within the college campus.
Aspect ratio: 9:16 (vertical); minimum frame rate: 30 FPS.
Minimum video resolution: 720 pixels; duration: 20–60 seconds.
The reel must be original, creative, and relevant to the event.
Background music, transitions and effects may be used in compliance with copyright guidelines.
Filming must not disrupt ongoing events or college activities. Obtain consent before prominently featuring individuals.
The reel must be posted on Instagram, tagging @damodar_college, and submitted to the organising committee by 10:30 AM on Day 2.
Participants are responsible for plagiarism and copyright violations in their submissions.
The organising committee may disqualify entries that are inappropriate or fail to comply with the rules.
The decisions of the judges and organising committee shall be final and binding.
judging: Creativity and Originality – Original concept, storytelling and creative execution – 15 marks
Coverage of Day 1 – Effective representation of activities, highlights and memorable moments – 15 marks
Editing and Technical Quality – Shot quality, transitions, audio and overall editing – 10 marks
Overall Impact – Visual appeal and effectiveness in conveying the event atmosphere – 10 marks
Total – 50 marks

competitions.name: TeamVerse
competitions.subtitle: Digital Identity Showcase
competitions.team: All members in video · 1 at screening
competitions.tagline: The opening showcase: introduce your whole team in a 3–4 minute video, without revealing your college.
competitions.overview: A creative yet technically driven introductory event that challenges teams to present their members and collective talents through a short digital video. It celebrates innovation, collaboration, storytelling and technical finesse while strictly maintaining institutional anonymity, and serves as the opening showcase of TechNation, setting the tone for creativity and excellence.
competitions.statement: Through this video you need to introduce all the members of the team. Every team member appears in the video, and any one member must be present during the screening. Submit it through the provided submission link (Google Form) by the deadline stated in the brochure (13 January, 2:00 PM); a confirmation email follows by 14 January, 11:30 AM. If a video is rejected for identity disclosure, one final resubmission is permitted by 15 January, 2:00 PM. Missing the resubmission deadline results in zero marks.
rules: Video Duration
- Only one video submission per team is allowed.
- The duration of the video should be 3–4 minutes per team.
- Videos exceeding or falling short of the specified duration may be penalised or rejected.
Video Format & File Size
- File name format: TeamVerse_Imaginary_Team_Name.mp4 (an imaginary team name such as Alpha, Beta, etc.).
- Accepted video format: MP4. Maximum file size: 200 MB.
- Recommended resolution: 1080p (Full HD) and not less than 720p (HD).
- Aspect ratio: 16:9.
- Audio must be clear and audible, with no copyrighted background music unless royalty-free and acknowledged.
Anonymity & Identity Disclosure
- The video must not show or mention your college name, logo, uniform, or any branding. Any identity reveal will lead to rejection.
Submission Guidelines
- The video must be submitted only through the provided submission link on or before 3rd January, 2:00 PM.
- A confirmation email acknowledging the submission will be sent by 4th January before 11:30 AM.
- If a video is rejected due to identity disclosure, one final resubmission will be permitted.
- The resubmission must be completed by 5th January, 2:00 PM, as specified in the confirmation email.
- Failure to meet the resubmission deadline will result in zero marks.
judging: Marks will be awarded for team participation and time-duration compliance, creativity, originality, and the overall impression created by the video.
Video quality, use of special effects, and technical presentation will also be considered during evaluation.
The judges' decision will be final and binding to all.

competitions.name: QBIT
competitions.subtitle: Innovate & Pitch
competitions.tagline: Pitch a technology-driven startup idea that solves a real societal, environmental or industry problem.
competitions.overview: QBIT inspires undergraduate students to conceptualise, innovate and present technology-driven startup ideas that address contemporary societal, environmental and industry-specific challenges. Participants integrate advanced technological concepts and demonstrate critical thinking, feasibility and entrepreneurial insight in their pitch.
competitions.statement: Prepare a structured 10–15 slide pitch deck covering: the problem statement; the proposed tech solution (innovation, working model, technological components); target audience or market segment; business / revenue model; prototype or system workflow (optional but strongly encouraged); and a feasibility & impact assessment. Suggested domains include AI & ML, IoT, cloud, cybersecurity, FinTech, HealthTech & MedTech, EdTech, robotics & automation, bioinformatics & biometrics, green/clean tech, Agri-Tech, big data & analytics, mobile and web computing, GPS and location-based services, recommendation systems, smart sensor networks, AR & VR, drones and UAVs, edge computing, wearables, blockchain and NLP.
rules: Ideas must be technology-driven and address a real-world problem. Participants may explore any relevant domain, including (but not limited to):
- Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning
- Big Data & Data Analytics
- Internet of Things (IoT)
- Mobile and Web Computing
- Cloud Computing
- GPS and Location-Based Services
- Cybersecurity Solutions
- Recommendation Systems
- Financial Technologies (FinTech)
- Smart Sensors
- Healthcare & MedTech
- Augmented Reality (AR) & Virtual Reality (VR)
- Educational Technologies (EdTech)
- Drone and UAV-based Solutions
- Robotics & Automation
- Edge Computing
- Bioinformatics & Biometric Technologies
- Wearable Technologies
- Green / Clean Technology Innovations
- Blockchain Applications
- Agricultural Technologies (Agri-Tech)
- Natural Language Processing (NLP)
Ideas must be original, innovative and technology-driven, with a clear connection to a real-world problem.
Plagiarism or misrepresentation of another person's work will result in disqualification.
Participants must acknowledge sources for data, statistics, visuals and other external material.
Each team must prepare a 10–15-slide professional presentation and submit it to the faculty event coordinator before the deadline.
The pitch must be delivered in English and must adhere strictly to the time limit communicated by the organisers.
A question-and-answer (Q&A) round will follow every presentation.
Participants are expected to maintain professional conduct, discipline and ethical behaviour throughout the competition.

Topics will be allotted based on the registration sequence of institutions. Once registered, teams will receive an official communication from the Event Teacher In-charge for topic selection. Teams must confirm their chosen topic via email/WhatsApp to the student and/or faculty coordinators.
The judging panel's decision will be final and binding.
Format for Tech Startup Pitch Presentation: each team must prepare a professional pitch deck of 10–15 slides, structured clearly and following the sequence below:
- Title and Team — Start-up name, tagline, team members and a concise description of the idea.
- Problem Statement — Define the real-world problem, who experiences it and why it matters. Support the problem, where possible, with credible evidence.
- Proposed Technology Solution — Explain the proposed innovation, how it works and which technologies enable it.
- Target Users / Market Segment — Identify the intended users, beneficiaries or customers and their needs.
- Value Proposition and Differentiation — Explain what makes the solution useful and how it differs from existing alternatives.
- Prototype / System Workflow — Use a demo, wireframe, flowchart, mock-up or concept sketch to show the user journey or system workflow. A prototype is strongly encouraged.
- Feasibility and Implementation — Describe the resources, skills, infrastructure and key steps required to develop and deploy the solution.
- Business / Sustainability Model — Explain how the start-up could generate revenue or sustain its operations. For non-commercial or social-impact ideas, explain the sustainability plan.
- Impact and Scalability — Describe the expected social, environmental or industry impact and how the idea could expand to reach more users.
- Conclusion — Summarise the idea and state the support, partnership, pilot opportunity or next step being sought.
- References — List sources for facts, statistics, images and other external material used.
Submission Guidelines
- The participating team has to prepare a 10–15 slide professional presentation and email it to the faculty event coordinator on or before the submission deadline.
- The presentation and pitch must be delivered strictly in English.
- Participants may include references for data, visuals, or statistical insights used in the presentation. However, copying content is prohibited and will result in disqualification.
- A mandatory Question-and-Answer (Q&A) round will follow each presentation.
judging: Innovation & Originality — 10 points
Relevance and Potential Impact of the Problem Identified — 10 points
Technical Feasibility & Practical Application — 10 points
Quality of Presentation and Communication Skills — 10 points
Ability to Respond Effectively During Q&A — 10 points

competitions.name: Code-a-thon
competitions.subtitle: Rapid AI Build (Hackathon)
competitions.tagline: Four hours to build and present a working full-stack web or mobile app with AI tools.
competitions.overview: A 4-hour challenge where participants build a full-stack web or mobile app using AI tools. Teams plan, develop and present a working prototype based on the given theme. The event promotes creativity, teamwork and the practical use of AI in real-world development.
competitions.statement: Build a working prototype on the theme announced at the start, within four hours, on your own laptop. Submit a zipped folder of the entire project with a README that states the project title, the tech stack (frontend / backend / database) and how AI tools were used.
rules: The project must be developed during the event and must follow the theme announced at the beginning.
Teams must consist of a maximum of 2 members. All members must be present throughout the event.
Participants must bring their own laptops and arrange their own internet connectivity (mobile hotspots permitted). Wi-Fi will not be provided by the organisers.
All development work must be completed within the 3-hour time limit.
Each team will get 5 minutes to present their project to the judges.
Submitting plagiarised work or presenting a pre-built project as original work will result in disqualification. Standard libraries and frameworks are permitted.
The use of USB drives is strictly prohibited.
The decision of the judges and organisers is final.
Submission Guidelines
- Submit a zipped folder of the entire project along with a README file.
- The README must include the project title, tech stack (frontend/backend/database), and how AI tools were used.
judging: Technical Implementation — 15 marks
Innovation & Originality — 10 marks
Design & User Experience — 10 marks
Effective Use of AI — 10 marks
Working Prototype — 3 marks
Presentation & Explanation — 2 marks

competitions.name: Tech-Persona
competitions.subtitle: Voices of IT
competitions.tagline: Dress up, speak up and become a legend of IT for eight minutes.
competitions.overview: Portraying IT personalities: four minutes of speaking followed by four minutes of questions from the judges, all answered in the style of the chosen personality.
competitions.statement: Once a team registers, the Team Leader is sent a list of personality names to choose from. The participant dresses up and presents in the speaking style of the chosen IT personality, using the video clips provided to learn about them.
rules: Once a team registers, the Team Leader will be sent options of personality names to choose from, to portray the character of an IT personality.
The participant has to dress up and present himself/herself in the speaking style of the chosen tech personality.
The participant will be provided with video clips relevant to the tech personality for learning about and portraying the personality.
Each participant will be given 4 minutes to present himself/herself, followed by questions from the judges about the tech personality.
Questions from the judges are to be answered in the same style as the portrayed tech personality.
The participant has to research the personality and answer the judges' questions (no material will be shared by the organisers for this).
Decisions of the judges and organisers will be final and binding to all.
judging: Total — 50 points
Relevant Costume and Style — 10 points
Portraying Chosen Tech Personality (Vocabulary and Speaking Style) — 20 points
Knowledge about the Tech Personality — 10 points
Overall Response to Questions from Judges — 10 points

competitions.name: Tech-Hire
competitions.subtitle: Simulated Tech Interview
competitions.rounds: Round 1 MCQ test · Round 2 Technical interview (top 5)
competitions.theme: Tech job roles allotted by lots
competitions.tagline: A simulated technology job interview: 20 MCQs, then a face-to-face panel for the top five.
competitions.overview: A simulated technology job interview where participants experience a real-world recruitment process. Round 1 – MCQ Test: Participants answer 20 multiple-choice questions based on a randomly allotted tech role, assessing technical knowledge, logical reasoning and problem-solving skills. Round 2 – Technical Interview: The top five participants face a face-to-face interview with a panel of judges, involving technical concepts, practical scenarios and HR/behavioral questions. Evaluation is based on technical knowledge, analytical thinking, problem-solving, communication and professionalism
competitions.statement: Job roles are allotted using lots: Software Tester (manual testing, Selenium and Postman); Graphic Designer (Canva, Photoshop and the Adobe suite); AI and Data Analytics (Python, machine learning and Power BI); UI/UX Designer (Figma, wireframing and prototyping); SQL Developer (MySQL, joins and database design). Round 1 is 20 MCQs for 20 marks in 20 minutes, subject to the organisers' decision. The top 5 qualify for Round 2, and the final ranking is based on Round 2 scores.
rules: Round 1 – MCQ Test
- All participants must appear for the MCQ test individually.
- Participants will be allotted the following job roles using lots:
- Software Tester (Manual Testing, Selenium and Postman)
- Graphic Designer (Canva, Photoshop and Adobe suite)
- AI and Data Analytics (Python, Machine Learning and Power BI)
- UI/UX Designer (Figma, wireframing and prototyping)
- SQL Developer (MySQL, joins and database design)
- The test will assess logical reasoning (debugging/coding), analytical thinking, problem-solving ability, and job-role-related knowledge.
- The questions will be based on the job role allotted to the participant.
- Round 1 consists of 20 MCQs for 20 marks in 20 minutes, subject to the organisers' decision.
- Participants must complete the test within the time allotted by the organisers.
- Each participant will be evaluated based on their individual performance.
- Based on the Round 1 scores, the top 5 participants will qualify for Round 2.
- If two or more participants obtain the same score, the organisers may use a tie-breaker question or a predetermined tie-breaker criterion.
Round 2 – Technical Interview
- The 5 shortlisted participants from Round 1 will qualify for the technical interview.
- Each shortlisted participant will attend a face-to-face interview conducted by a panel of judges.
- The interview will be based on the job role allotted in Round 1.
- Questions may include technical concepts, problem-solving tasks, practical scenarios, and HR or behavioural questions.
- Participants will be evaluated on:
- Technical knowledge
- Problem-solving ability
- Communication skills
- Confidence and professionalism
- Analytical and practical thinking
- Each participant must answer the questions independently.
- The final ranking will be based on the Round 2 scores.
judging: Round 1 — 20 points
Round 2 — 80 points (technical knowledge, problem-solving, communication, confidence and professionalism, analytical and practical thinking)
Total — 100 points

competitions.name: CodeRush
competitions.subtitle: Python Debug Duel
competitions.tagline: Find the bugs on paper, then code the solution in PyCharm.
competitions.overview: A coding and debugging programming event that tests coding accuracy, logical thinking and debugging efficiency using Python.
competitions.statement: Round 1 — Debugging / error identification: participants receive a printed Python code file containing errors, identify them and write the corrections. Only the top 5 move on. Round 2 — Coding: a problem statement with an expected result; code it in Python using PyCharm so the output matches. This round decides the Winner and Runner-up.
rules: Round 1 — Debugging / Error Identification
- Participants will receive a printed Python code file containing some errors.
- They must identify the errors and write the corrections.
- Only the top 5 participants will move to Round 2.
Round 2 — Coding
- Participants will be given a problem statement with an expected result.
- Coding should be done in Python using PyCharm. The output must match the expected result.
- This round will determine the Winner and the Runner-up.
judging: Accuracy of error identification and corrections (Round 1)
Correctness of output against the expected result (Round 2)

competitions.name: CineBytes
competitions.subtitle: Trailer Forge
competitions.theme: A 1–2 minute trailer from a 40-minute film
competitions.tagline: Cut a 40-minute film down to a 1–2 minute trailer in OpenShot.
competitions.overview: A 40-minute video (preferably animated) is provided. Based on this video, a trailer of 1–2 minutes needs to be created.
competitions.statement: All required files are given at the venue and there is no internet access. Using only OpenShot Video Editor and the given resources, create a 1–2 minute trailer within the allotted time.
rules: Participants must work independently on the allotted college computers. Everyone will receive the same source video at the official start. Sharing files, viewing another participant's project, receiving unauthorised assistance, or interfering with another participant's work is prohibited.
All video, audio, and title editing must be done using OpenShot Video Editor installed by the organisers. Using additional software or plugins is prohibited.

Participants must use only the provided video and its original audio. External music, sound effects, images, videos, externally sourced templates, pre-made projects, and other external content are prohibited. Participants may create their own text titles using OpenShot's built-in title templates during the competition.
AI tools and AI-generated content are prohibited.
Internet use, including mobile data and hotspots, is prohibited. Mobile phones, personal storage devices, and personal computing devices must not be used during the competition.
Participants must bring wired headphones or earphones with a 3.5 mm jack.
The trailer must be 90–120 seconds long, including all titles and credits, and should build interest in the supplied video.
Submit one final trailer in MP4 format at 720p resolution (1280 × 720).

The trailer must be fully exported, checked, and submitted before the 60-minute deadline. No separate viewing or additional rendering time will be provided. No editing, re-exporting, or replacement submissions are permitted after the applicable deadline.
Late, missing, unplayable, or non-compliant entries will not be judged. Violations of the competition rules may result in disqualification.
The judges' decision will be final and binding.
judging: Creativity & Originality — 30 marks
Story Flow & Scene Selection — 30 marks
Editing Skills, Pacing & Transitions — 25 marks
Technical Quality, Audio Balance & Title Readability — 15 marks
Total — 100 marks

competitions.name: UXplorer
competitions.subtitle: Design with Purpose
competitions.tagline: A real-world case study, Figma, and the clock: design an interface people would actually use.
competitions.overview: UXplorer is a UI/UX design challenge where creativity meets problem-solving. Participants receive a real-world case study with a design task and, using Figma, craft an intuitive and visually compelling user interface. The event also emphasises prototyping, turning ideas into interactive, user-friendly experiences.
competitions.statement: Design wireframes and a clickable prototype in Figma for the given theme, audience and problem, from scratch, within the event window.
rules: Participants must have knowledge of Figma.
Individual participation. No teams, no groups.
The theme will be provided on the day of the event.
Internet will be available. Participants are allowed to download images required for the design, and strictly not templates.
No pre-made templates, purchased UI kits, or copied full-screen designs are allowed.
All designs must be created from scratch during the event window.
Designs must reflect the given theme, audience, and problem.
Participants must complete the project within the allotted time, which typically includes:
- Wireframes
- Clickable prototype
Participants must follow standard UI/UX practices:
- User interface
- Prototyping
judging: Creativity & Originality — 20
User Experience (Flow & Functionality) — 20
User Interface (Visual Quality) — 20
Prototype & Interactions — 20
Presentation & Explanation — 20

competitions.name: QueryQuest
competitions.subtitle: From Tables to Triumph
competitions.tagline: Nested queries, complex sub-queries and a ticking clock.
competitions.overview: Query Quest is a database event where participants receive a dataset and must write SQL queries, including nested queries, to retrieve the correct data. It tests logical thinking, database knowledge and query-building skills.
competitions.statement: Write correct SQL for the given dataset, including nested and complex sub-queries, within the time limit, and submit the queries in a Notepad file.
rules: Queries must be written using correct SQL syntax for the given dataset.
Queries will also include nested and complex sub-queries.
Mobile phones and other electronic devices are strictly prohibited during the competition.
Internet access or external help is not allowed.
The time limit must be strictly followed.
In case of a tie, accuracy and execution time will be considered.
Queries must be submitted in a Notepad file.
The decision of the judges will be final.
judging: Accuracy of Query and Result — 20 points
Use of Correct SQL Syntax & Logic — 20 points
Time Management — 10 points

competitions.name: AdCraft
competitions.subtitle: Prompt the Vision. Create the Impact.
competitions.theme: A 1-minute video ad on the given theme
competitions.tagline: Generate every shot with Grok, cut it in OpenShot, and sell the idea in sixty seconds.
competitions.overview: A creative event that challenges participants to design a digital video advertisement entirely through effective prompting. Using Grok, participants generate visuals based on how clearly and creatively they prompt. It is a test of both creativity and smart AI usage.
competitions.statement: Create a 1-minute video advertisement on the given theme: generate multiple clips with Grok (grok.com/imagine), combine and edit them in OpenShot Video Editor, and add sound effects only from Pixabay. Save the final ad, all raw clips, audio and exported files in a desktop folder named after your team, and submit a Word document containing every prompt used.
rules: Accounts required: participants must create accounts on Grok (grok.com/imagine), Pixabay (pixabay.com) and OpenShot beforehand.
Participants must create a 1-minute video advertisement based on the given theme.
Participants must generate multiple clips using Grok and must use OpenShot Video Editor to combine, arrange, and edit these clips into the final advertisement.
Participants are allowed to use sound effects only from Pixabay, which must be added through the video editor.
No other websites, AI tools, or external software are permitted.
The judges' decision will be final and binding.
Any violation of the rules will result in immediate disqualification.
Eligibility Criteria
- Participants must have knowledge of OpenShot video editing software.
Submission Guidelines
- Participants must create a folder on the desktop named after their team.
- The final advertisement video must be saved inside this folder.
- All raw video clips, audio files, and exported files used in the project must be included in the same folder.
- A Word document must be submitted containing all prompts used in Grok.
judging: Prompt Creativity and Quality — clarity, originality, and effectiveness of prompts used to achieve the intended concept — 25 points
Visual Output and Clip Quality — relevance of generated clips to the advertisement theme — 25 points
Editing and Technical Execution — smooth clip joining, clean cuts, proper transitions and integration of sound effects to enhance the advertisement — 25 points
Message Clarity and Creativity — strength of the advertisement concept and clear communication of the message or product idea — 25 points

competitions.name: PowerBit
competitions.subtitle: Power the Data. Own the Insights.
competitions.tagline: Three hours, one dataset, a dashboard with real insights in Power BI.
competitions.overview: Data Analytics using Power BI is a 3-hour professional competition in which participants analyse datasets, build interactive dashboards and present meaningful insights. It develops industry-aligned analytics competencies while fostering critical thinking, visualisation skills and real-world problem-solving, cultivating future-ready data analysts.
competitions.statement: Topics, themes and datasets are provided on the spot. Submit a fully functional Power BI report (.pbix) with a PDF export of the dashboard and a brief 150–200 word summary of insights within the 3-hour window. The report should clearly reflect data cleaning, modelling, visualisation and insights.
rules: Participants must report to the venue on time.
Topics, themes, and datasets will be provided on the spot to ensure fairness and real-time analytical assessment.
The total duration of the competition is 3 hours, during which all work must be completed and submitted.
Use of the internet is restricted only to Power BI documentation and DAX references; browsing external dashboards or ready-made templates is strictly prohibited.
Participants must work only on the dataset provided; external data sources are not allowed.
Each participant/team must submit the Power BI (.pbix) file and a PDF export before the deadline.
Dashboard designs must be original. Plagiarism or use of pre-built templates will result in immediate disqualification.
Judges' decisions will be final and binding.
Any form of malpractice, technical manipulation, or disturbance during the event will lead to disqualification.
Submission Guidelines
- Participants must submit a fully functional Power BI report (.pbix file) along with a PDF export of the dashboard.
- All submissions must be uploaded within the allotted 3-hour competition window. Late submissions will not be evaluated.
- The Power BI report should clearly reflect data cleaning, modelling, visualisation, and insights.
- Participants must ensure originality; plagiarism or pre-built dashboards are strictly prohibited.
- Each submission should include a brief explanation or summary of insights (150–200 words).

competitions.name: CypherCell
competitions.subtitle: Investigate. Connect. Crack
competitions.tagline: Two minds, one hour, a trail of digital clues: crack the case first.
competitions.overview: Teams of two get exactly one hour to solve a series of digital puzzles and clues that help crack a digital forensics case.
competitions.statement: Solve the puzzles in sequence on the systems provided. The team that cracks the case first within the hour, with all previous puzzles solved correctly, wins. If no team cracks it, the team that solved the most clues correctly is declared the winner.
rules: Each team must consist of exactly 2 members.
Each team will be given exactly 1 hour to solve a series of digital puzzles/clues that help crack a digital forensics case.
Calculators, mobile phones or any external gadgets are not allowed.
Teams must maintain decorum; any form of cheating, brute force or tampering with the systems provided will lead to immediate disqualification.
The event coordinators reserve the right to modify or update rules or terminate participation in case of emergencies, logistics, safety concerns or rule violations.
Decisions made by the event coordinators will be final and binding.
judging: The team that cracks the case first within the time limit of one hour (provided all the previous puzzles given to the team have been solved correctly) will claim victory.

If none of the participating teams is able to crack the case within the stipulated hour, the teams will be judged on their accuracy in solving and decoding the clues/puzzles. The team that solved the most clues/puzzles correctly will be declared the winner.

competitions.name: Mortal Kombat 11
competitions.subtitle: Kombat Showdown
competitions.tagline: Best of three, first to two rounds, until only one fighter stands.
competitions.overview: Mortal Kombat 11 is a visceral fighting game with a cinematic story, brutal combat and iconic characters. With customisable variations, stunning visuals and competitive play, it delivers intense battles, fatalities and strategic depth.
competitions.statement: Players for the final round are drawn by lots. Sets are best of 3 matches (finals optionally best of 5), first to 2 rounds per match, competitive mode enabled. An odd draw forms one round-robin group of three whose top two join the single-elimination bracket; everyone else plays 1v1 knockouts.
rules: Mode: Versus
Selection method: players for the final round are chosen by drawing lots (random selection).
Final round: all selected players compete in a knockout format until the champion is decided.
Player eligibility
- Accounts: only one account per player.
- Attendance: players must be present at the draw and at match start.
Match format
- Set format: best of 3 matches (first to 2 wins), finals optional best of 5.
- Rounds per match: first to 2 rounds (MK11 default).
- Competitive mode: enabled (tournament-legal variations, standardised frame data).
- Characters: any character allowed; the winner may switch only after the opponent switches (or enforce winner-lock, organiser's choice).
- Stage select: random; stage interactables: on (organiser may set off if preferred).
- Timer: default.
- No macros/cheats: controller remapping allowed within game settings only.
Tournament structure
- Lots draw
- Random selection: the organiser draws lots to determine which players enter the final round.
- Variable size: the number of players may vary based on attendance.
- Odd number of players adjustment
- Group of three: if the draw yields an odd number, form one group of 3 players.
- Group stage: the 3 players play a round-robin (each faces each opponent once, best of 3 sets).
- Advancement: the top 2 from the group (based on wins, then game differential, then head-to-head) advance to the knockout bracket.
- Knockout bracket: all other players (outside the group of 3) play 1v1 in a single-elimination bracket (best of 3 sets).
- Integration: after the group stage, the two advancing players join the ongoing knockout bracket at the appropriate round.
- Final round
- Single-elimination: continues until one champion remains.
- Small draws: if only 2 players are drawn → direct final.
- Bracket sizing: if more players are drawn → create quarterfinals/semifinals as needed.
Code of conduct
- Sportsmanship: respect all participants and organisers; no abusive language or unsportsmanlike behaviour.
- Pauses: only for legitimate issues (controller disconnect, health/safety); notify the organiser immediately.
Organiser rights
- Control: manages the lots draw, group stage, and bracket creation.
- Final say: has decisive authority on disputes and rulings.
- Rule adjustments: may adjust rules before the tournament begins, but not mid-match.
judging: Match results in the group stage and knockout bracket

competitions.name: RC Car Gaming
competitions.theme: RC cars in an enclosed arena
competitions.tagline: Push, flick and rebound the ball into the goal with your RC car.
competitions.overview: RC cars score goals in an enclosed arena: standard 2v2 or 1v1 depending on arena size and team. Cars push or flick the ball with their chassis and bumpers; a goal is awarded whenever the ball completely crosses the goal line.
competitions.statement: Matches run for 5 minutes of regulation time. If the score is tied, a 30-second shoot-out follows: the attacker gets 15 seconds to drive from centre and score, each team takes turns (best of 3 shots), and sudden-death rounds decide a winner if still tied.
rules: General Setup
- Standard 2v2 / 1v1 depending on arena size and team.

- No out-of-bounds: because the arena is completely enclosed in a cage, the ball is always live. If there are walls, players can use the walls and ceiling to make indirect passes or rebound shots. If no walls exist, there will be a defined boundary; once the ball crosses the boundary the timer is paused, the ball is kept in the centre and the timer resumes.
- Scoring: a goal is awarded whenever the ball completely crosses the goal line. Once scored, the clock pauses, the ball is reset to the centre circle, and play resumes on the referee's whistle.
- Passing & dribbling: cars must push or flick the ball using their chassis/bumpers. Holding, trapping, or pinpointing the ball under a car frame for more than 3 seconds is considered stalling.

- Penalties & violations: deliberate pinning/sticking: if a car intentionally traps the ball against a wall or corner for more than 3 seconds to stall time, a free kick is awarded to the opponent from the centre. A player will be disqualified if this happens more than 3 times.
Eligibility
- Players must be present at the time of the draw and match start.
Match Incidents
- Aggressive tipping / flipping: unintentional collisions are part of the game. However, intentionally trapping or flipping an opponent's RC car upside down results in direct disqualification.

- Technical issues / vehicle flip: if an RC car flips over on its own or suffers technical failure, the match continues. Organisers will flip the RC car upright at the nearest pause or safe moment without stopping the main timer.
judging: Tie-breaker rule (sudden death / penalty shoot-out)
- Trigger: if the score is tied at the end of the 5-minute regulation time.

- Format (30-second shoot-out): the ball is placed at the designated spot, and the attacking player's RC car is placed behind it. The attacker gets 15 seconds on the clock to drive from the centre and score a goal. Each team takes turns (best of 3 shots). If still tied, sudden-death single rounds apply until a winner is decided.

faqs.a: TechNation 2027 runs {dates} at {venue}. All events are conducted offline on the campus.

Participation is by invitation to recognised colleges and institutions across India. It is open to undergraduate students of BCA, B.Sc. (Computer Science / IT), B.Voc. (Software Technologies / Software Development) or equivalent IT-related programmes, who are bonafide students of their institution.

faqs.q: How many students can a college send?
faqs.a: One team per college or institution, with 10 to 12 students, all from the same institution. Teams may assign different participants to different events to avoid schedule clashes. Each team must be accompanied by a Faculty Coordinator and a Student Team Leader.

The team registration fee is ₹3,000 per team and covers all events. Pay by bank transfer to VVMS Shree Damodar College of Comm. & Eco, HDFC Bank, Goa Margao branch, account number 50100150767879, IFSC HDFC0000037.

Register your team through this website and confirm participation at least one week before the event dates. For queries write to cs.sdcc@vvm.edu.in or call the faculty coordinators, Mr. Sumit Kumar (+91 98221 67259) or Mr. Ramkrishna Reddy (+91 88065 72120).

faqs.q: What do we need to bring on the day?
faqs.a: A deputation letter issued by your institution and valid college ID cards of all participants, to be produced at the registration desk on 8 January 2027. Laptops are needed for Code-a-thon and an audio-listening device for CineBytes.

faqs.q: Why can't we show our college name?
faqs.a: To keep evaluation fair and unbiased. Every team receives a unique Team Name at the venue, and no college name, logo, insignia or branded material may be worn, displayed or carried until the results are announced at the valedictory on 9 January. Violations can mean penalties or disqualification.

Accommodation is the responsibility of the participating team, but the organising committee can provide limited assistance and guidance on prior request. Local transport between the designated hotel and the venue is arranged by the host, and breakfast and lunch are provided on both days.

First and second prize winners of each event receive trophies and e-certificates (or printed certificates). Points are awarded for participation and positions, and the teams with the highest cumulative points receive the Overall Winner and Overall Runner-Up trophies at the valedictory ceremony.

All official communication, including event schedules, rules and announcements, is sent to the registered email of the Team Leader or Faculty Coordinator. Event-specific instructions are shared before each event starts.
